key_insight: The paper shows that large language models contain highly specialized functional subnetworks that can be selectively updated to enable continual learning with less catastrophic forgetting.
engineering_relevance: For AI system design, the method offers a targeted, parameter-efficient way to adapt models over long training sequences while preserving prior capabilities.
method: Use gradient-attribution profiling to identify cognition-associated subnetworks with low mutual overlap.
Route each training example to its corresponding subnetwork and restrict weight/optimizer updates to those regions.
Apply CiMEO (Function-isolated Memory-Efficient Optimization) for localized continual adaptation.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 1.4 million sequential instructions across five generative benchmarks, CiMEO achieved the best average performance among compared methods while reducing forgetting.
watch_item: Subnetwork routing and overlap assumptions may depend on reliable task-to-subnetwork assignment, so misrouting or changing task boundaries could reduce the method’s benefit.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
